items.title: 【分享】零 API key：我讓 DSH 用自己的瀏覽器開 Google 搜尋，搜完自動關分頁
items.excerpt: 新人首貼，分享一個最近搓出來的小工具。 起因 DSH 內建的 web_search 走官方搜尋 API。我機器上本來就裝了 ego-browser（ego lite）——一個人和 agent 共用的瀏覽器，agent 能用我真實的登入態。某天想到：既然瀏覽器就在本機，何不讓 agent 自己開 Google 搜？不用申請 API key、不用搜尋訂閱，查詢只在自己瀏覽器裡跑，不經過第三方搜尋服務。 於是寫了這個 provider：接上 DSH 的搜尋介面，把預設搜尋換成「ego-browser 開 Google」，順手開源。 效果 裝好之後，下一次 web_search 就走這條路。每次搜尋的完整過程： 開一個獨立 task space → 載入 Google 結果頁 → 抽取有機結果（標題、連結、摘要、發布日期）→ 關閉 space 和所有分頁 → 把結果回傳給 agent。 實測體感： 一次搜尋約 2 秒。結果乾淨：標題＋連結＋摘要＋日期，「3 天前」這種相對日期也會換算成實際日期。 agent 一次丟多個查詢時，內部限流最多開 2 個瀏覽器，其餘排隊，不會一口氣炸出十個分頁。 搜完不留分頁、不留暫存檔，不弄髒你的瀏覽器。 官方搜尋 provider 保留，設定頁隨時切回；這個插件只改預設。 零依賴、零安裝腳本，純 JS，裝完即用。 幾個老實的限制 只有有機連結，沒有官方那種…

items.title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility
items.excerpt: Large language models(LLM) show promise for strategic reasoning, yet their ability to compute game-theoretic equilibria under dynamic conditions remains largely unexplored. This work investigates whether fine-tuned LLMs can serve as solver-free surrogates for online equilibrium computation in honeypot allocation, a setting in which network mobility continuously reshapes the underlying attack graph and forces repeated re-solving of a two-player zero-sum game. items.title: Backbone-Specific LoRA Geometry: Orthogonality, Superposition, and Provenance
items.excerpt: Sharing one low-rank adaptation (LoRA) update across pretrained models simplifies deployment. Composition methods typically combine updates from a common backbone, while cross-model transfer transforms updates for a target backbone. The conditions for sharing updates across backbones while preserving accuracy and distinguishing individual contributions remain unclear. Our idea is to use backbone-specific update directions as signatures of their training backbones. items.excerpt: State-of-the-art multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) models rely on large pretrained encoders, yet typically process every modality to its full depth, regardless of its computational cost or predictive contribution. This raises a fundamental question: how should limited computation be allocated across modalities to preserve predictive performance? We reveal a substantial mismatch between the computational cost of modality encoders and the predictive benefit of processing them more deeply, suggesting that different modalities require different encoding depths. items.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
items.excerpt: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. items.excerpt: Predicting holo-like protein conformations from apo structures is essential in structure-based drug design.
